elements.justification: “truck” and “combination of vehicles” are terms DEF-NRS-484A-305 and DEF-NRS-484A-050 define and the run admits as the aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck and DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles, so the span claims ru.aggregate with each id and never the class atoms ru.truck or ru.trailer_or_combination, which the aggregate's exclusion forbids as a substitute. The width is kin.extent, “the body's size along its axes about the reference point: a trace writes the half-length, half-width and half-height; a formula reads the full length, width and height, twice each”, whose width read is the overall width the words measure; the literal 80 inches is the law's own figure and is declared in literals. “driver” is read through controlled motion (narrowing on this span).

“which is following” is a relation between two road users over time and maps to drv.interaction.following, built on rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, “a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction”, and rel.same_direction. The followed road user is of the same two defined terms, claimed as the same admitted aggregates, with kin.extent's width read for the combination; the followed road user is quantified inside the applicability and the obligation and is no binder, since the duty exists for the subject whether or not a scene supplies one.

“a space of 500 feet” is the clear distance between the two bodies: rel.surface_gap is “distance between the nearest points of two bodies, each body's footprint read with its own heading and extent: zero when they touch or overlap, never negative; its longitudinal and lateral components are the lengths of the vector between those nearest points along and across the subject's heading”, so its longitudinal component is the space the words measure, and its exclusion of a centre-to-centre reading is why rel.centre_distance is not used, that atom being “not a stand-in for a clearance between bodies”. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane fixes that the space is the one ahead of the subject towards the vehicle it follows. The figure 500 feet is the law's own and is declared in literals.

“overtaking and passing” is a relation between road users over time and maps to drv.interaction.overtaking, which states the same direction within a tolerance, a speed excess and the bodies drawing level (rel.same_direction, kin.speed, rel.longitudinal_overlap, rel.ahead_behind_in_lane). The three defined terms of the span claim their admitted aggregates: the overtaking road user as truck or combination, the overtaken as vehicle or combination.

“any vehicle or combination of vehicles” claims the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles. “while moving” is the negation of drv.motion.standstill, the posted definition of complete cessation from movement read as a motion state. “on a highway” is st.highway, “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic” — DEF-NRS-484A-095 word for word — anchored to the subject by rel.occupies and tied to the lanes by st.on_way, “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, shoulder …”. “two or more lanes available for traffic moving in the same direction” is st.lane, “a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles”, with st.lane_adjacency, which carries “lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction”, the count the words require, and st.lane_direction, “direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in”, which fixes that the direction counted is the one the subject travels in; st.lane_adjacency's exclusion “not a stand-in for the marking between two lanes” does not apply, the words counting lanes and not markings. “available for traffic” is carried by those two lane atoms themselves: a region of kind st.lane is by its kind a strip of roadway for one line of vehicles and by st.lane_direction carries a designated direction of travel, which is what makes a counted lane one available for traffic moving in that direction. No ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic claim is made of the subject: the words make traffic the road users for whom the lanes are available, not a class the subject must carry, and the class the exception puts on the subject is the vehicle or combination its own words name, which the span already claims — a subject that is a vehicle moving on a highway is traffic of DEF-NRS-484A-285 by that definition's own words (“vehicles … using any highway for purposes of travel”) wherever the rest of this exception holds, so the claim would decide nothing anywhere and is not made.

operationalizations.convention: Traffic-flow feasibility convention (free-flow versus congested operation in highway capacity practice): leaving and holding a long space ahead is possible only where the stream runs freely and nothing occupies or closes the space. The conditions permit at an observation where the subject's kin.speed, “magnitude of velocity”, is at least p.conditions_permit_min_speed, so that a queue or stop-and-go running is not read as a failure to leave the space; where the number of road users that occupy a roadway the subject occupies (rel.occupies with st.roadway) between the subject and the road user it follows — ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) and at a smaller longitudinal rel.surface_gap than that road user — is at most p.conditions_permit_max_intervening_users, so that a vehicle that has moved into the space is not read as the subject's closing of it; where no st.obstruction, “a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user”, lies on the highway the lane the subject occupies lies on (st.lane, rel.occupies, st.on_way, st.highway) nearer to the subject's body than that longitudinal gap, the distance read through st.region_geometry, which carries “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”; and where no dev.temporary_traffic_control, “cones, barricades, temporary signs and flashers marking works, a closure or an obstruction”, governs a lane or roadway the subject occupies — dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls”, which is the atom that ties a device to the subject, a device quantifier being otherwise unanchored — since a works zone or a closure of the subject's own lane makes the space impossible to hold. Both magnitudes are parameters of the reading; the words state none.

residues.why: The purpose clause explains the figure the law itself fixes: the space is 500 feet, and the words “so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger” state what that space is for, adding no further requirement to the duty, which is met by leaving the stated space and breached by not leaving it. The ontology reads a purpose through the conduct it explains, and here that conduct is the leaving of the space the next words measure. The rule is held to this: no verdict of the node turns on these words.

applicability: The bound road user is a truck of DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck, or a road user of DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles whose read width is at least the literal 80 inches, and it is following (drv.interaction.following) some other road user that is likewise a truck or a combination of that width. The subsection does not apply where the subject, a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle or a combination, is moving (not at a standstill) on a highway it occupies through a lane of that highway on which the count of lanes in the lane's direction of travel is at least the literal two (s7), nor where the subject is overtaking and passing another vehicle or combination (s6).
obligation: At each observation at which the applicability holds and the conditions of s3 permit, the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap between the subject and the road user it is following must be at least the literal 500 feet. The followed road user is re-selected in the obligation with the whole of the s2 selection, since the applicability's quantifier does not reach it, and the space is owed to each road user so selected. Where that gap is below the figure the duty is violated; where the gap, or a quantity the conditions of s3 read, is unobserved the duty is unknown.

narrowings.why: “The driver of any truck or combination of vehicles” is read as that truck or combination, the road user whose motion is controlled: who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads “the driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion.

The standard's convention relieves the duty where the space itself cannot be held, and the vocabulary places neither a structure region nor a device inside the space between two bodies: st.region_geometry carries the unsigned ground distance from the subject's body to a region and st.on_way ties that region to a highway and to no stretch of it, while dev.governs ties a device to a travel region and not to a length of one. The obstruction leaf is therefore read as an st.obstruction on the highway the subject's lane lies on and nearer to the subject's body than the road user it follows, which also reads an obstruction that distance behind the subject, and the works-zone leaf as a dev.temporary_traffic_control governing a lane or roadway the subject occupies rather than one standing in the space ahead. Both readings make the conditions not permit in some scenes in which the words would still require the space.

The space of 500 feet is read as the longitudinal component of the clearance between the two bodies, measured along the subject's heading from the nearest point of its own body to the nearest point of the body ahead, which is the quantity the vocabulary carries for a space between vehicles; a centre-to-centre distance would overstate the space by about the two half-lengths.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a two-lane rural highway with one lane in each direction, an articulated lorry runs at 22 m/s about 60 m behind another articulated lorry in the same lane, headings aligned. No road user is between them, no obstruction lies on the way and no temporary traffic control governs their lane or roadway, and the subject is well above the free-flow speed, so the conditions permit; the longitudinal gap is far below 500 feet.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same two lorries on the same highway at the same speed, with nothing in or across the space, but the follower holds a longitudinal gap of about 260 m, which exceeds 500 feet.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car — neither a truck of the truck aggregate nor a coupled combination, and 70 inches wide — follows an articulated lorry at 60 m on the same two-lane highway. The subject is outside the classes the subsection binds and the rule does not engage.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The forbid scene with the source declaring the gap between bodies absent: both road users' classes, the following relation and the single-lane carriageway are recorded, but the space cannot be read, so the duty is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The same two lorries at 60 m, moving on a dual carriageway whose lane adjacency records three lanes in the direction of travel of the lane they occupy. The second exception applies by its own words and the subsection does not apply.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: On the two-lane highway the following lorry is overtaking and passing the lorry ahead: the two travel in the same direction, the follower's speed exceeds the leader's by 4 m/s and the lorry ahead is still ahead of it in the lane as it draws level. The first exception applies and the duty does not bite on the closed space.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The follower lorry is held at 2 m/s in a slow-moving queue on the two-lane highway, 15 m behind the lorry ahead, with a van that has moved into the space between them. Its speed is below the free-flow bound and a road user occupies the space, so the conditions do not permit and no space of 500 feet is owed at that observation.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: The forbid geometry at free-flow speed with nothing between the two lorries, but a line of cones — a temporary traffic control device — governs the lane the subject occupies, a works zone on its own lane. The conditions do not permit, so the shorter space is not a breach at that observation.

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: The subject lorry runs alone at 22 m/s on the two-lane highway: no other road user is in the scene, so it follows nothing, the trigger fails and the subsection never engages — a decided verdict in a scene that supplies none of the road users the rule quantifies over.

param_proposals.name: p.conditions_permit_min_speed
param_proposals.convention: Traffic-flow feasibility convention: the speed below which running is queued or stop-and-go, so that holding a long space ahead is not possible, taken from the boundary between congested and free-flow operation.
param_proposals.source: speed-flow curves and congested-regime boundaries in highway capacity practice

param_proposals.name: p.conditions_permit_max_intervening_users
param_proposals.convention: Traffic-flow feasibility convention: the number of other vehicles that may occupy the space ahead before the subject is read as unable to hold it, since a vehicle that moves into the space closes it without any act of the subject.
param_proposals.source: gap-closure observations in heavy-vehicle platooning field trials
